engineeringScope.scope: Derived model quantities, not measured engine data. Operating lines are actual component matches, not an engine test sweep. Static thrust power is zero; jet kinetic power is not thermal efficiency. No modeled surge margin.

performance.environment: Fresh Linux Chromium profile on dedicated CDP port 9337, warm server, ANGLE SwiftShader, forced WebGL; single cold-client run
performance.reproduce: CHROME_WS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9337 GOWORK=off go run ./cmd/gosx perf --json --coverage --frames 45 --timeout 60s --budget examples/turbofan/perf-budget.json --budget-profile turbofan-engineering 'http://127.0.0.1:8096/?model=jt9d&backend=webgl'

limitations: Three fitted ground points; one unfitted public comparison, not blind validation.
Modeled low-speed map extensions and aggregate efficiency corrections are not manufacturer measurements.
Estimated shaft RPM and station states lack independent measurements.
Steady component matching; no CFD, metal-temperature model or transient shaft dynamics.
Geometry is schematic and does not determine the numerical component maps or nozzle areas.
Software WebGPU device loss recovered through WebGL2; native WebGPU parity remains unverified.
Canonical shared checkout; consumed build artifacts and example sources are identified by hashes, with framework HEAD recorded at capture.
Station h/s/cp/gamma and temperature–entropy paths use frozen air-equivalent gas; no reacting-mixture or chemical-equilibrium model.
The operating-line sensitivities are secants between neighboring model samples, not measured or exact analytical derivatives.
Application data requests are absent during control checks; ordinary framework telemetry POSTs are recorded separately.
